description.label: THE PROGRAM
description.title: WRESTLING IN DAGESTAN
description.p1: In Dagestan, wrestling is not a sport. It is an identity. Every village has its champion, every family passes on its techniques, and a serious wrestler logs 5,000 hours of mat time before turning 18. This region produces more Olympic wrestling champions per capita than anywhere else in the world.
description.p2: The MKR program gives you access to that knowledge: freestyle wrestling exclusively, in the real gyms, with the Caucasus-specific techniques you will not find in any European academy. And coaches able to fix in seconds what you have been doing wrong for years.

faq.label: QUESTIONS
faq.title: BEFORE APPLYING TO THE WRESTLING CAMP

items.question: Do I need to already be a good wrestler to train in Dagestan?
items.answer: No, but you need a base: minimum 1 year of regular practice in wrestling, grappling, BJJ, judo or MMA, with real ground work. Instruction happens by demonstration, at the local pace: without that base you cannot follow, and you break down within the first week. Your level is confirmed on the video call with Ruslan before validation, and sparring groups are organised by level once on site.

items.question: What will I learn that I cannot find in Europe?
items.answer: Three things. The Caucasus signature techniques: leg rides, chain wrestling, chained mat returns, rarely taught in Europe. The volume: 2 sessions a day, 6 days a week, with more serious sparring rounds in 2 weeks than in 6 months at an average European club. And the corrections: coaches who have seen thousands of versions of every move and fix in seconds what you have been dragging for years.

items.question: What does a typical week look like at the Wrestling camp?
items.answer: 6 training days, 1 rest day. Every day: a 10:30 session (technique, drills, situations) and a 17:30 session (competition intensity, directed sparring), with recovery and meals in between. On rest day, optional excursion: Sulak Canyon, Sarykum Dune or Gamsutl village. All of it with MKR liaisons around.

items.question: Can my child really train in Dagestan?
items.answer: Yes, from 8 to 17, provided a parent takes part in the camp (that is the Family track). Kids have their own program with a dedicated youth coach, a 1-to-5 coach ratio, separate sessions at 10:30 and 17:30 and never any free sparring. Parents can attend every session. This is where the local champions all started as kids.

items.question: Who will I train with?
items.answer: With local wrestlers of regional to national level depending on the session, in the partner gyms of Makhachkala and Kaspiysk. Partners are used to foreign athletes and calibrate the sparring: in Dagestan, controlled sparring is a coach's pride, not a free-for-all. MKR liaisons are on the mat with you.

items.question: What is included in the camp price?
items.answer: The package covers the Russian visa (full application handled by MKR), the Istanbul-Makhachkala domestic flight, transfers, housing, 2 meals a day and the 2 daily training sessions. On your side: the flight to Istanbul, your travel insurance and your equipment. The rate depends on group size and duration (1 to 3 weeks): the full grid is public on the Sessions page.

faq.label: QUESTIONS
faq.title: BEFORE APPLYING TO THE MMA CAMP

items.question: What exact level do I need for the MMA camp in Chechnya?
items.answer: Advanced level minimum: 5+ years of regular practice, or competition experience (regional, national or international). The application form automatically blocks lower levels when you choose MMA, and Ruslan confirms every profile on a video call. The reason is simple: your sparring partners are professionals and the pace of the sessions assumes a real technical base.

items.question: Who do I actually spar with in Grozny?
items.answer: With the fighters of Grozny's professional teams and their new generation, in MKR's partner gyms. These are athletes who make a living from MMA, supervised by their coaches during the sessions. Sparring is calibrated: coaches adjust the intensity to your level, round after round. Demanding, never reckless.

items.question: What does a typical day look like at the MMA camp?
items.answer: Two sessions a day, 6 days a week: 11:00 and 18:00. Every session follows the same loop: warm-up, technique of the day, drills, sparring in 5-minute rounds, then an individual debrief by the coach. Between sessions: meals, recovery, treatment. On rest day, optional excursion or full recovery.

items.question: Why Chechnya rather than Thailand?
items.answer: They are two different products. Thailand offers camps open to everyone, striking-oriented, in a tourist ecosystem. Grozny offers a complete wrestling-based MMA, a density of professional sparring partners you will not find anywhere else, and zero tourists on the mat. If your goal is MMA competition and your ground game needs to grow, the Caucasus is the most direct option.

items.question: What about safety in Grozny?
items.answer: Two honest sentences: Western governments advise against travel to Russia, Chechnya included, and you should know it. On the ground, Grozny is a tightly controlled city where foreign athletes are respected, and MKR manages everything: permanent liaisons, pre-departure briefing, 24/7 emergency contact, mandatory repatriation insurance. Full details are on the Chechnya destination page.

items.question: I come from wrestling or grappling with no real striking: MMA or Wrestling?
items.answer: If you have 5+ years on the mat and want to add the MMA dimension (striking, cage, transitions), the MMA camp is built for that: stand-up can be taught, and your ground base will make the difference. If your goal is to sharpen your pure wrestling, choose the Wrestling camp in Dagestan. In doubt, ask on the video call: Ruslan frames your profile before validating.
